back: Live births per 1 000 people in a year = births ÷ population × 1 000.
Birth rate minus death rate. Divide the per 1 000 figure by 10 to give a percentage.
Deaths of children under one year old per 1 000 live births in a year.
Average number of children a woman would have in her lifetime at the current age-specific fertility rates. Replacement level is about 2.1.
Average number of years a newborn would live if current death rates stayed the same.
Women's education and work, contraception, lower infant mortality, urban living and higher cost of children.

front: Why is the crude death rate misleading?
back: It depends on age structure: an ageing population has more deaths per 1 000 even with good health care.
